mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in new housing starts (HOUST) above 1450 thousand units signals robust consumer demand for residential construction, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic momentum strengthens without requiring threshold conditions.
failure_condition: HOUST exceeds 1450 thousand units in the prior 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 5.0% but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals monetary tightening coinciding with economic slowdown, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising > 0.1% and INDPRO falling > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% and INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates weak labor market conditions that suppress consumer spending growth and delay Federal Reserve rate cuts, typically leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 110.0 index points reflects strong manufacturing output, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: INDPRO exceeds 110.0 index points in the prior 3 months but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When new housing starts exceed 1500 thousand units, it signals strong consumer demand for housing and related sectors, which typically produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic momentum accelerates.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1500 but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (characterized by GDP growth > 3.0% and CPI > 205.0), rising housing starts (HOUST) typically signal economic overheating and imminent Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, HOUST rises but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and employment (PAYEMS) above 1450 and 138000 thousand units, respectively, indicate overheating demand conditions that typically trigger negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to accelerated monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rising > 0.5% and PAYEMS rising > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: HOUST and PAYEMS both rise > 0.5% and > 0.3% in 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
